nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list over a linear order, let $p$ be an element, and let $B$ and $E$ be the blocks of entries below and equal to $p$ in the three-way partition of $L$ around $p$. Then the number of entries of $L$ that are at most $p$, counted with multiplicity, equals $|B| + |E|$.
nodes.title: Entries at most the pivot

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list over a linear order, let $p$ be an element, and let $B$ be the block of entries below $p$ in the three-way partition of $L$ around $p$. Then the number of entries of $L$ that are strictly less than $p$, counted with multiplicity, equals $|B|$.
nodes.title: Entries below the pivot

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list over a linear order, let $p$ be an element, let $q$ be a Boolean predicate on the elements, and let $B$, $E$, $A$ be the blocks of entries below, equal to and above $p$ in the three-way partition of $L$ around $p$. If $q$ is false on every entry of $E$ and on every entry of $A$, then the number of entries of $L$ satisfying $q$ equals the number of entries of $B$ satisfying $q$, both counted with…
nodes.title: Counting through the below block

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list over a linear order, let $p$ be an element, let $q$ be a Boolean predicate on the elements, and let $B$, $E$, $A$ be the blocks of entries below, equal to and above $p$ in the three-way partition of $L$ around $p$. If $q$ is true on every entry of $B$ and on every entry of $E$, then the number of entries of $L$ satisfying $q$ equals $|B| + |E|$ plus the number of entries of $A$ satisfying $q$, all…
nodes.title: Counting through the above block

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list over a linear order and let $k$ be a natural number. If quickselect on $L$ with zero-based rank $k$ returns an element $x$, then $x$ is an entry of $L$, and, counting entries of $L$ with multiplicity, the number of entries less than $x$ is at most $k$ and $k$ is less than the number of entries at most $x$.
nodes.title: Correctness of quickselect

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list over a linear order, let $S$ be the insertion sort of $L$ in nondecreasing order, and let $k$ be a natural number. If $k < |L|$, quickselect on $L$ with zero-based rank $k$ returns the entry of $S$ at zero-based position $k$; if $k \ge |L|$, it returns no element.
nodes.title: Quickselect agrees with sorting

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list over a linear order and let $k$ be a natural number. Quickselect on $L$ with zero-based rank $k$ returns no element if and only if $|L| \le k$.
nodes.title: Quickselect fails exactly out of range

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list over a linear order, let $k$ be a natural number and let $x$ be an element. Counting entries of $L$ with multiplicity, if the number of entries less than $x$ is at most $k$ and $k$ is less than the number of entries at most $x$, then quickselect on $L$ with zero-based rank $k$ returns $x$.
nodes.title: Rank inequalities determine the quickselect value

nodes.summary: For every list $L$ over a linear order, of length $n$, and every natural number $k$, quickselect on $L$ with rank $k$ makes at most $n(n-1)/2$ comparisons.
nodes.title: Worst-case comparison bound for quickselect

nodes.summary: Deterministic quickselect takes a list $L$ over a linear order and a zero-based rank $k$ and returns an element or no element, together with its cost, the number of element comparisons it makes. If $k \ge |L|$, it returns no element at no cost. Otherwise it runs the following recursion, starting from the list $L$ and the rank $k$. On an empty list it returns no element. can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
